body: 2021 was then India's best-ever year for IPO fundraising (Business Today year-ender). By 30 Dec 2021, 45 of 65 IPOs were above issue and 15 had doubled - the 'listing pop' peak. The marquee loss-making tech listings then de-rated in 2022: Paytm (issue Rs2,150, Nov-2021, largest IPO to that date) was at ~Rs864 (-60%) by Feb 2022 and later fell further; Nykaa (issue Rs1,125, listed ~Rs2,206, peaked ~Rs2,573) was ~21% below issue (bonus-adjusted) in 2023; PB Fintech (issue Rs980, +22.7% on day one) ~22% below issue by Feb 2022; Zomato (issue Rs76, peaked ~Rs169) fell >50% to ~Rs82 by Feb 2022 before turning into a large winner by 2024 as quick commerce scaled and it turned profitable. LIC (May-2022, issue Rs949) listed at Rs867 (-8.6%). Client Associates' later study found companies 'with clear profitability paths, revenue scaling, and margin improvements significantly outperformed', while cash-burning firms lost value. Lesson: in a hot vintage, the issue price embeds the peak multiple; the long-run outcome then splits on whether unit economics turn positive (Zomato, PB Fintech recovered; Paytm suffered a regulatory blow in Jan-2024 RBI action on Paytm Payments Bank). Early signal visible at the time: losses + high OFS share (PE/VC exits) + price set on revenue multiples. Prices quoted are snapshot values from dated articles, not current.

data.early_signals: losses, OFS-heavy, revenue-multiple pricing, record subscription
data.lesson: vintage peak multiples; outcome splits on unit economics

title: India's 2021 IPO vintage: record fundraising, then new-age tech fell 40-75% - profitability path separated survivors

body: Form 13F-HR: institutional managers with >= $100M in 13(f) securities report long US-listed equity/option positions within 45 days of quarter end. Not included: shorts, cash, bonds, most non-US holdings; confidential treatment can delay positions. So a 13F is a stale (up to ~4.5 months), partial snapshot. Data since 2013 is XML; the value field switched from thousands to whole dollars in Jan-2023 (handled in sec_fetch.py). Test 20-Nov-2026: Berkshire 13F for 30-Sep-2026 (filed 16-Nov-2026) parsed to 30 positions, $304.2B, top Apple 25.0%, American Express 15.2%, Coca-Cola 11.3%. Evidence (to verify before citing numbers): the academic work on managers' 'best ideas' (Cohen-Polk-Silli 2010) finds their highest-conviction positions outperform while diversified remainder does not; activist 13D filings (>5% with intent, now due within 5 business days after 2023 amendments) show positive announcement returns (Brav-Jiang-Partnoy-Thomas 2008). Uses: find what concentrated, long-horizon managers own in small caps; check crowding (many funds in one name = exit risk); track 13D/13G stake changes. Don't clone mechanically: lag, survivorship of famous managers, and position size context are missing.
title: 13F filings: useful for idea sourcing and crowding checks, weak as a copy-trading signal
